clue.text: Clumsy phrase for angelic creature

indicators.note: a clumsy arrangement is a botched one, so the letters of the next word are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone mocks an awkward turn of phrase used to describe a heavenly being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clumsy' looks like a comment on the phrase's style, but it tells you to rearrange PHRASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraph is one of the highest order of angels in Christian tradition.

clue.text: Late for an unspecified occasion

explanation.definitionFit: Sometime can mean former, as in 'the sometime mayor', and also at some time not named.

clue.text: A rude — no, fragmentary-piece of verse

indicators.note: broken into fragments, so the letters of the preceding words are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone refuses a coarse poem, calling it a broken scrap of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fragmentary' breaks A RUDE NO into pieces to be rebuilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a short French poetic form with a refrain, built on two rhymes.

clue.text: Prophet, helping Archie to achieve his aims?

definitions.text: helping Archie to achieve his aims?

explanation.surface: A seer assists a man called Archie with his ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Archie' was British wartime slang for an anti-aircraft gun; the predictor was the device that calculated where to aim it.
explanation.definitionFit: One who foretells events is a prophet, and the anti-aircraft fire-control instrument bore the same name.

clue.text: A musical connexion in use tonight, we hear

explanation.surface: Someone mentions a musical link that will be used at this evening's event.
explanation.walkthrough: In music an accolade is the brace joining staves; it is also the touch of a sword that confers knighthood, and 'tonight' said aloud is 'to knight'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bracket joining several staves in a score bears the name, as does the ceremony of dubbing a knight.

clue.text: Funny mistakes demonstrated by players

parts.note: the players are actors, and the comic blunders they show are the title of a Shakespeare play

explanation.surface: Amusing errors made by sportsmen during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's farce of mistaken identity about two sets of twins is literally a play of amusing blunders.

clue.text: What the sodium-discoverer lived in (E. Clerihew Bentley)

definitions.text: What the sodium-discoverer lived in (E. Clerihew Bentley)

indicators.note: the answer lives inside the word for the element, tucked within its letters

explanation.surface: A literary question about the home of the chemist who found sodium, citing a comic poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Bentley's clerihew says Sir Humphry Davy 'lived in the odium / Of having discovered sodium', and the word sits inside 'sodium' itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatred and disgrace aimed at a person is what Bentley's verse says Davy lived under.

clue.text: Rewrite Poe, said Fatty

indicators.note: rewriting the words puts their letters down again in a different order

explanation.surface: An editor tells someone nicknamed Fatty to redraft some Edgar Allan Poe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fatty' looks like a nickname being addressed, but it is the definition, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose tissue is the body's fat-storing tissue, so the word describes something consisting of fat.

clue.text: Make effective use of net work

definitions.text: Make effective use of net work

parts.words: Make effective use of net work
parts.note: using a net well means catching something in its meshes, so 'net work' is read as the work a net does

explanation.surface: Advice to get the most out of networking.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch or entangle something as if in a net is what a fisherman's mesh is for.

clue.text: For these American sailors Plymouth was home from home

definitions.text: For these American sailors Plymouth was home from home

parts.words: For these American sailors Plymouth was home from home
parts.note: the settlers sailed from Plymouth in England and founded Plymouth colony in Massachusetts, a second home bearing the old name

explanation.surface: US navy crews feel at home when docked in the Devon port.
explanation.walkthrough: They are not sailors in the naval sense but the Mayflower passengers of 1620, who left Plymouth in Devon and founded Plymouth in New England.
explanation.definitionFit: The English Puritan settlers who crossed on the Mayflower are known collectively by this name.

clue.text: Law of inheritance men smiled about

indicators.note: turned about, so the letters of the two words are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Men grinned on hearing about a genetic principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but asks for MEN SMILED to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregor Mendel's principles of heredity, from his pea experiments, are the theory of genetic inheritance named after him.

clue.text: Where Helen lit up towers, improperly dressed?

definitions.text: Where Helen lit up towers, improperly dressed?

parts.words: Where Helen lit up towers, improperly dressed?
parts.note: Marlowe has Helen's face burn the 'topless towers' of Troy; topless also means improperly dressed

explanation.surface: Someone asks where a woman called Helen was seen half-naked, lighting up tall buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: Marlowe's Faustus asks if Helen's face 'burnt the topless towers of Ilium'; topless, of a person, means improperly dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilium is the Latin name for Troy, the city burned in the war fought over Helen.

clue.text: Prolific place for starting game, China-style

parts.note: in golf each hole is started from the tee
Ming is the Chinese dynasty whose porcelain style is famous

explanation.surface: A fertile spot for opening a match played in a Chinese manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarming and abundant, as a river teeming with fish is plentiful in life.

clue.text: Drupes for mother and children, ren

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, as in horse breeding
sons are children

explanation.surface: Plums handed out to a mother and her offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: A drupe is a fleshy fruit with a stone, and these small dark plums are an example.

clue.text: Doctor last to lose his hair ?

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, an army doctor
ult. is short for ultimate or ultimo, meaning last

explanation.surface: A physician is the final one to go bald.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals shed hair or feathers seasonally, the way a dog casts its coat.

clue.text: Alone on Italian island with Edward

parts.note: isola is the Italian word for island
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A man named Edward is by himself on an island off Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Set apart, cut off from others, as a remote house stands on its own.

clue.text: An extremity, with respect to an Italian appetizer

parts.note: a tip is an end or extremity
'as to' means regarding or with respect to

explanation.surface: Someone talks about the end of a starter at an Italian meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian first course of cold meats, olives and the like comes before the pasta.

clue.text: Rattling good instrument-or how to 8?

explanation.surface: Someone praises a percussion instrument and asks how to do something.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is ENMESH: to catch in a net you cast a net, which read as three words gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The clicking shell-shaped clappers of Spanish dance make a rattling noise; casting a net is how a fisherman catches.

clue.text: Way into estate-simple perhaps but costly

definitions.text: Way into estate-simple perhaps but costly

parts.words: Way into estate-simple perhaps but costly
parts.note: an entry is a way in, and a fee simple is an estate held outright in law, so the costly way in is read in two senses

explanation.surface: Getting into a country house may be straightforward but it is expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: A fee is, in law, an inherited estate (as in 'fee simple'), so an entry to a fee is literally a way into an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: The charge for admission is the price paid to go in somewhere.

clue.text: Remedy for a noisy guitarist ?

explanation.surface: A cure is sought for a guitarist who makes too much noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO STRUM, it is the instruction you would give a loud guitarist.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack medicine or pet cure-all is a remedy; telling a guitarist not to strum would quieten them.

clue.text: Article at back of letter in Greek

parts.note: 'the' is the definite article

indicators.note: taken back, so the little word at is read the other way round

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece printed on the back of a letter written in Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' looks like correspondence with something on its reverse, but 'letter in Greek' is the definition and 'at back' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth character of the Greek alphabet is a letter in that script.

clue.text: Going for an away match

parts.note: the match is a marriage and away means running off, not a fixture at the other side's ground

explanation.surface: A team travelling to play at the opposition's ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The sporting 'away match' is a marriage made after running away together.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers who run off secretly to marry are making a match away from home.

clue.text: About five a depression is coming

indicators.note: the outer pieces go about, around, the Roman number

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Weather forecast: about five days and a low-pressure system will arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts A DENT around V. 'Depression' looks like weather, but it is a dent.
explanation.definitionFit: The arrival of something long awaited, and the church season before Christmas marking Christ's arrival.

clue.text: Come down and get rid of the smell ?

explanation.surface: Someone climbs down and then airs the room to remove a bad odour.
explanation.walkthrough: As DE-SCENT it would mean removing the scent.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop or climb downward is a coming down; split as de-scent it is the removing of an odour.

clue.text: Foreign articles of earlier origin

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for 'the'
der is the German word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Imported goods that date from an older period.
explanation.definitionFit: Older, born earlier, as the senior of two siblings is.

clue.text: Sympathy for strike at harbour

parts.note: to rap is to hit or strike
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: Support is offered to dock workers on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A close understanding and harmony between people is a fellow feeling.

clue.text: Eric the Red, in extremis, went wrong

indicators.note: only the extremities of the phrase are kept, so its middle stretch is dropped

explanation.surface: The Viking explorer, at the point of death, made a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in extremis' usually means at the point of death; here it keeps the ends, ER and RED, losing the middle letters ICTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have made a mistake is to have strayed from what is right.

clue.text: Somehow Green is so, outgoing

indicators.note: done in some unknown way, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A comment that a person called Green is, oddly, sociable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outgoing' looks like a personality trait, but it means going out.
explanation.definitionFit: Egression is the act of going out, an exit or departure.

clue.text: In Scotland Tom takes a chance on a seaside shrub

parts.note: Tam is the Scottish form of Tom
a risk is a chance taken

explanation.surface: A Scotsman called Tom gambles on a coastal bush.
explanation.definitionFit: A feathery evergreen bush that grows well in salt winds on coasts.

clue.text: No thug, however bad, is a cipher

indicators.note: however badly they are put, the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that a thug, however wicked, is a nonentity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cipher' means zero here, not a code.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero, the figure 0, is called a cipher in older usage.
